skill.name: risk-metrics-calculation
skill.description: Calculate portfolio risk metrics including VaR, CVaR, Sharpe, Sortino, and drawdown analysis. Use when measuring portfolio risk, implementing risk limits, or building risk monitoring systems.
skill.summary: Calculate portfolio risk metrics, drawdowns, risk-adjusted returns, and stress test workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Portfolio risk reviews need consistent VaR, CVaR, drawdown, and risk-adjusted return calculations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through clear risk metric patterns.
actual_capabilities: Calculates volatility, VaR, CVaR, drawdown, and downside deviation from return series.
Compares portfolio return, portfolio volatility, component risk, and diversification ratio.
Builds rolling risk views for volatility, Sharpe ratio, VaR, and maximum drawdown.
Supports historical, hypothetical, and Monte Carlo stress test workflows.
Explains risk-adjusted metrics such as Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, Omega, and information ratio.
Provides implementation patterns using Python, pandas, NumPy, and SciPy.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete audited risk system.
It requires clean return series, benchmark data, and portfolio weights from the user.
It does not validate market data quality or fetch prices automatically.
It is not financial advice or regulatory certification.

use_cases.title: Measure Daily Portfolio Risk
use_cases.description: Calculate VaR, CVaR, drawdowns, and risk-adjusted returns for a live portfolio review.

use_cases.title: Build Risk Tooling
use_cases.description: Implement reusable Python classes for core metrics, rolling analysis, portfolio risk, and stress tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare Risk Reports
use_cases.description: Create consistent metric summaries for limit monitoring, scenario analysis, and internal reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Basic Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to calculate volatility, VaR, CVaR, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, and maximum drawdown for my return series.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Portfolio Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare asset contributions to portfolio volatility with my returns table and target weights.

prompt_templates.title: Build Rolling Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design rolling risk metrics for a dashboard, including windows, formulas, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Stress Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create historical, hypothetical, and Monte Carlo stress tests for my portfolio assumptions.

output_examples.input: Daily returns for a multi-asset portfolio with a 95 percent confidence target.
output: Annual volatility estimate with clearly named assumptions.
Historical VaR and CVaR at the requested confidence level.
Maximum drawdown and drawdown duration summary.

output_examples.input: Portfolio weights and asset return history for five holdings.
output: Portfolio volatility and annual return estimate.

output_examples.input: A request to test portfolio losses during crisis and high-volatility periods.
output_examples.output: A stress test plan with selected scenarios, expected loss metrics, worst-case loss, and validation checks.

best_practices: Use several metrics because VaR, CVaR, drawdown, and ratios answer different risk questions.
Document lookback windows, confidence levels, annualization factors, and risk-free rate assumptions.
Validate results against benchmark data and known stress periods before using limits.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on VaR alone for tail risk decisions.
Do not assume returns are normal without checking skewness and kurtosis.
Do not mix return frequencies or annualization factors in one report.

faq.question: What data do I need?
faq.answer: You need a time series of returns. Portfolio analysis also needs asset returns, weights, and benchmark returns when relevant.

faq.question: Can it calculate Value at Risk?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook covers historical, parametric, and Cornish-Fisher VaR methods.

faq.question: Does it support CVaR?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes Expected Shortfall, also called CVaR, based on losses beyond VaR.

faq.question: Can I use it for dashboards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes rolling volatility, rolling Sharpe ratio, rolling VaR, and rolling drawdown patterns.

faq.question: Does it fetch market prices?
faq.answer: No. You provide prepared return data, benchmarks, and portfolio weights.

faq.question: Is this financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It is an implementation aid for calculations and reporting workflows.
